normative_clauses.heading: ## E1 — strict repeated-epoch context composition
normative_clauses.rule: A successor context must bind the predecessor new configuration, exact next epoch, retained ancestry endpoints and every consecutive ancestry edge before returning a verification-only context.

normative_clauses.heading: ## 6. Epoch seals and checkpoint finality
normative_clauses.rule: An epoch handoff must retain authenticated old and new context and cannot infer live activation from a local context object.

authenticated_inputs: Predecessor and successor strict activation authorities and the complete retained header ancestry.
preconditions: Successor old validator set and parameters equal predecessor new values; successor epoch is the checked next epoch; retained ancestry is nonempty and endpoint-bound.
accepted_effects: Return the supplied successor as a verification-only context after exact parent, height, genesis, chain and protocol checks.
rejected_effects: Configuration, epoch, endpoint, parent, height or context substitution returns ValidationError without creating a Core or signer authority.
uncertain_recovery: No durable write is performed by this operation; any interrupted caller must reconstruct both complete authorities and retry the identical composition.
publication: No Safety transition, signing lease, persistence ACK or first-new-block capability is published.

errors.meaning: A malformed or substituted successor context or retained ancestry is rejected before any authority is created.
Missing retained ancestry is local unavailability for this bounded verification operation, not peer Byzantine evidence.

cases.expected_outcome: Real Ed25519 successor activation, handoff quorums and retained ancestry compose into a strict repeated-epoch context.
A same-context substitution is rejected and cannot be mistaken for a successor epoch.
assertion_fragments: expect_err("a repeated epoch context must never be accepted as a successor")
successor old context differs from predecessor new context

independent_vectors.reason: The repository fixture uses real signatures but independently authored byte vectors, crash cuts and external custody evidence are not supplied.

open_requirements: Safety14/Core first-new execution, signer custody, application checkpoint carry-over and two-successive-epoch live activation remain open.
Independent epoch byte/signature vectors and multi-host/HSM recovery remain open.

normative_clauses.heading: ## T1 — finalized transaction to state-sync binding
normative_clauses.rule: Join only fresh finalized-transaction and state-sync readbacks whose block, height, state-root, binding and manifest identities agree; the join is not an atomic finality transaction.

normative_clauses.heading: ## M13 — State Sync / Light Client / Proofs
normative_clauses.rule: A state-sync readback carries partial progress and cannot claim finality or a complete snapshot without the existing verification capability.

authenticated_inputs: A finalized transaction owner readback and a durable native state-sync store owned by separate lifecycles.
preconditions: Both owners return fresh readbacks; block, height, state root, binding digest and manifest digest must match exactly.
accepted_effects: Return a domain-separated joined binding containing the exact finalized transaction identity and current sync progress digest.
rejected_effects: Any identity substitution returns a typed Sync error; finality and state-sync owners are not rewritten by the join.
uncertain_recovery: A sync readback failure may follow durable finality; reopen both owners and retry the exact read-only join, never submit a second transaction.
publication: The result is a candidate binding only and cannot claim finality, complete snapshot verification or production listener activation.

errors.meaning: A finalized state-root or block substitution is rejected before a binding digest is returned.
A state-sync readback error can occur after finality is durable and requires exact recovery/retry.

cases.expected_outcome: Matching finalized and state-sync readbacks produce a joined digest with exact block, root and progress identity.
A substituted state root or block ID returns the corresponding deterministic mismatch and no joined digest.

independent_vectors.reason: Bridge tests are source regressions; independent transaction bytes, authenticated finality sources and listener/network evidence are not supplied.

open_requirements: The two-owner join remains non-atomic and candidate-only; production RPC/listener, authenticated network source and complete-snapshot proof are open.
An end-to-end crash cut after durable finality and before sync readback requires a commissioned host.

normative_clauses.heading: ## S1 — incremental SQLite state-sync append and crash recovery
normative_clauses.rule: Chunk and metadata progress update in one SQLite transaction, require fresh readback, accept exact duplicates and reject substitutions or stale writers.

normative_clauses.heading: ## M13 — State Sync / Light Client / Proofs
normative_clauses.rule: The durable native state-sync owner validates each chunk and metadata identity before allowing progress to escape.

authenticated_inputs: An open native state-sync session, its manifest and a chunk whose index, bytes and manifest digest are authenticated by the session.
preconditions: SQLite namespace identity, binding and manifest match the session; chunk index and byte limits are within the selected profile.
accepted_effects: One BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction writes the exact chunk and metadata progress, then fresh readback confirms the new state.
rejected_effects: Duplicate identity is read-only; substituted chunk, stale concurrent writer, wrong manifest or disconnected checkpoint leaves the durable source unchanged.
uncertain_recovery: A process killed during an uncommitted append reopens at the exact source progress; resume only the identical valid chunk after readback.
publication: Append progress is not a finality receipt, trust anchor or complete snapshot capability.

errors.meaning: Chunk, manifest, ordering or session substitution rejects without partial progress.
A SQLite write or readback error requires reopen and exact source/target classification before retry.

cases.expected_outcome: A durable append survives a child-process reopen, while tampered progress readback is rejected.
A stale second writer cannot replace a durable chunk or advance metadata.
SIGKILL during an uncommitted SQLite append leaves zero chunks and exact source progress; a valid append then resumes.

independent_vectors.reason: SQLite process-crash evidence is real but independently authored bytes, physical power-loss/controller-cache tests and external rollback authority are not supplied.

open_requirements: Physical power-loss and controller-cache durability, independent host rollback floors and scalable incremental compaction remain open.
A production peer transport and authenticated complete-snapshot verifier remain separate requirements.
